note: v0.5.0 is released. E6.1 is done (T7 waits for a first deprecation), E6.2 is done (the GitHub round trip passes locally against a throwaway registry; running it in CI needs the E2E_REGISTRY variable and E2E_GITHUB_TOKEN secret, see the workflow file), and the docs audit is done. What is left: cut v1.0.0-rc.1, install it with brew and the script, and run the round trip against it (E6.3-T2), then tag v1.0.0 and check the tap and signatures (E6.3-T3). Work goes on a branch and a pull request; push to main only when the owner asks.
risks: Docs must continue to avoid implying that Hikma AI itself is a canonical skill registry; it is the CLI that works with user-configured registries.
Tests for global installs must never touch the real home directory (E4.2-T8).
Claude personal skills do not load in cloud or Cowork sessions, so global installs do not help in a Codespace; the global-install docs must say so up front (E4.2-T3).

Agents disagree on a skill that exists at both scopes and mostly do not document it. Checked 2026-10-17: OpenCode 1.19.0 is unstable (project or global), Codex 0.133.0 lists both with project first, Copilot untested. Docs say documented, reported, or checked, never a winner beyond Claude Code.
E6.1 adds public promises (exit codes, JSON schemas, config version) that cannot change before 2.0; the council run (E6.1-T5) must come before any of it is built.
gh skill was a public preview and may change; E6.2-T4 adds a canary so interop breakage shows up before users report it.

The automated checks prove behavior, not looks. Not judged by a person: how the menu and colors look in the Windows legacy console and a light terminal theme, and how the home page feels on a real phone. Look when convenient; none of it blocks the tag.
Bash completion needs bash 4.1+ and bash-completion; macOS bash 3.2 and Git Bash cannot run it. Documented in the completion page; PowerShell is the Windows answer.
